title: Molecules with ALMA at Planet-forming Scales (MAPS). VI. Distribution of the Small Organics HCN, C<SUB>2</SUB>H, and H<SUB>2</SUB>CO
question: Characterize the spatial distribution, column densities, and excitation temperatures of the small organic molecules HCN, C2H, and H2CO on planet-forming scales in five protoplanetary disks.

data.angular_resolution: 0.15'' (15-24 au) for 3-2 lines; 0.3'' (30-48 au) for 1-0 lines and tapered 3-2 / H2CO lines

what.value: Source characterization parameters (spectral type, distance, inclination, position angle, stellar mass)

evidence.quote: Reproduced from (cite: oberg21), where additional source characteristics and a list of references are provided.
The stellar masses needed to compute the Keplerian velocities are taken from (cite: oberg21) and are estimated from gas dynamics in (cite: Teague21).

what.value: Spectroscopic constants and partition functions for HCN, C2H, and H2CO

evidence.quote: The spectroscopic constants are taken from the CDMS database (cite: cdmsA; cdmsB) for HCN, and from the JPL database (cite: jpl) for C$_2$H and H$_2$CO.
Measurements are provided by (cite: Ahrens2002) for HCN, by (cite: Sastry1981) and (cite: Padovani2009) for C$_2$H, and by (cite: Bocquet1996) for H$_2$CO.

external_data.citation: CDMS (cite: cdmsA; cdmsB), JPL (cite: jpl), (cite: Ahrens2002), (cite: Sastry1981), (cite: Padovani2009), (cite: Bocquet1996)

what.value: Gas temperatures inferred from peak brightness temperatures of 12CO 2-1 and 13CO lines, and emission surface heights

evidence.quote: We thus restrict the rotational temperature between 10 K and the gas temperature inferred from the peak brightness temperature of the optically thick $^{12}$CO 2–1 line, $\rm{T}_{\rm{gas}}$($^{12}$CO) (cite: law21_surf), for both HCN and C$_2$H.

what.value: CO column density profiles derived from C18O 2-1, CO snowline locations, and total water ice mass inside 50 au

evidence.quote: Figure 6 shows the normalized column density profiles of HCN, C$_2$H, and H$_2$CO, as well as the CO column densities derived from the C$^{18}$O 2–1 line by (cite: zhang21).
The light blue vertical lines in the bottom panels of Fig. 6 mark the estimated location of the CO snowline in each disk as measured by (cite: zhang21).

evidence.loc: Small organics reservoir in the inner 50 au
evidence.quote: The total water mass inside $50$ au was estimated from the models presented in (cite: zhang21), and are listed in Table 1 of (cite: oberg21).

what.value: Positions of dust continuum gaps and outer edge of the continuum disk

evidence.quote: The position of the dust continuum gaps, as measured by (cite: law21_rad), are marked by the gray dashed vertical lines in Fig. 6.

recipe.goal: Generate zeroth-moment maps and measure disk-integrated line fluxes
recipe.method: Integrate velocity channels to create zeroth-moment maps and compute disk-integrated fluxes using elliptical masks based on disk inclination, PA, and observed emission extent.
key_parameters: Disk inclinations and position angles from Table 1

recipe.goal: Extract deprojected radial intensity profiles and radial spectra
recipe.method: Deproject zeroth-moment maps using GoFish radial_profile and extract Keplerian-shifted deprojected spectra in radial bins of 1/4 beam major axis using GoFish radial_spectra.
key_parameters: Radial bin size = 1/4 of the beam major axis
Averaging wedge = 30 degrees along disk major axis (or full azimuthal average for low S/N: C2H in IM Lup and GM Aur, and H2CO in all sources)

recipe.goal: Retrieve HCN and C2H column density and excitation temperature profiles
recipe.method: Two-step LTE hyperfine spectral fitting with thermal line width flux redistribution: first simultaneously fit 0.3'' 1-0 and tapered 3-2 spectra to constrain Tex,0; second fit 0.15'' 3-2 spectra using priors around Tex,0 (and fixed CO temperatures in inner blended regions).
key_parameters: Free parameters: N_tot, FWHM line width Delta V, excitation temperature T_ex, velocity offset v_lsr
Background temperature T_bg fixed to max(continuum brightness temperature, CMB 2.73 K)
assumptions: Local thermal equilibrium (LTE), beam filling factor of 1, and identical excitation temperature for all hyperfine components
Flux computed with purely thermal line width and redistributed over observed broader line width to account for beam smearing

recipe.method: Fit a single Gaussian to the 0.3'' H2CO 3_03-2_02 line in each radial bin under LTE for fixed excitation temperatures between 20 and 50 K.
key_parameters: Fixed excitation temperatures T_ex between 20 and 50 K
assumptions: LTE and excitation temperature between 20 and 50 K

recipe.goal: Estimate inner 50 au organic gas and ice masses and abundances relative to water
recipe.method: Integrate column density profiles within r < 50 au (extrapolating inward at constant column density where inner disk fits fail), multiply by an ice-to-gas ratio of 1000, and divide by modeled water ice mass inside 50 au.
assumptions: Constant column density extrapolation inward in the inner disk where fits are poor

evidence.quote: We derive column density and excitation temperature profiles for HCN and C$_2$H, and find that the HCN emission arises in a temperate ($20 - 30$ K) layer in the disk, while C$_2$H is present in relatively warmer ($20-60$ K) layers.
HCN temperatures range from 20 to 30 K, while C$_2$H temperatures range from 20 to 60 K.

evidence.quote: HCN temperatures range from 20 to 30 K, while C$_2$H temperatures range from 20 to 60 K.
